title: Bribery: The Sin We Stopped Noticing
subtitle: 2:188, 5:42 and two hadiths

content.alt: Bribery: The Sin We Stopped Noticing

content.text: Bribery is a major sin in Islam. In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:188):

content.alt: وَلَا تَأْكُلُوا أَمْوَالَكُم بَيْنَكُم بِالْبَاطِلِ وَتُدْلُوا بِهَا إِلَى الْحُكَّامِ لِتَأْكُلُوا فَرِيقًا مِّنْ أَمْوَالِ النَّاسِ بِالْإِثْمِ وَأَنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ (Qur'an 2:188)

content.text: "Do not consume one another's wealth unjustly, and do not offer it to the authorities so that you may knowingly and sinfully take a part of other people's wealth."
Allah also describes people who are سَمَّاعُونَ لِلْكَذِبِ أَكَّالُونَ لِلسُّحْتِ
"eager listeners to lies, greedy eaters of what is forbidden"
(5:42). The word سُحْت (
suht
) covers unlawful earnings, and the early scholars named bribery as one of its clearest examples.
It has become normal

Whenever I visit the subcontinent and other developing countries, I see how deep this goes. Many of us who grew up there do not think twice when we go back. A small payment to skip a queue, to get a job, a loan, a plot of land, a contract, a vote. It has even reached the arrangements for Hajj.
I once watched a man who had just finished Umrah and i'tikaf pay a porter to jump the long check-in line for the flight home. I am sure he did not think much of it. I could not believe my eyes.
Who is the bigger sinner?
Many people think only the one who takes the bribe is guilty. The Prophet ﷺ made no such difference:
Both are cursed:
'Abdullah ibn 'Amr reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it (Tirmidhi 1337).
Especially in judgment:
Abu Hurayrah reported that he cursed the one who gives and the one who takes a bribe to sway a judgment (Tirmidhi 1336).
And Allah knows best.
